IncidentBot: PAGING: gpu-48 (us-west-2) — repeated CUDA/Xid 79 resets + ECC correctable count spike. Multiple inference containers restarted automatically. Paging @Oncall GPU :rotating_light:

Ana (SRE): ack. I'm on it. Initial telemetry shows 6 resets in the last 3m, node went NotReady briefly. Taking ownership for initial triage.

Oncall GPU: taking. TL;DR: customer-facing latency spike reported ~2m ago, some requests 5-10s higher. No full service outage yet.

Dev Patel: logs from the runtime show contiguous kvcache OOM logs before the resets. Could be memory pressure + soft ECC corrections escalating. Posting relevant tail:
```
2026-03-15T21:18:02 runtime[pid=2141]: kv_cache: alloc failed size=384MB
2026-03-15T21:18:03 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3e:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
2026-03-15T21:18:03 containerd: task runtime-infer: exit status 137
```

Kai (Runtime): interesting — exit 137 usually OOM killed or driver reset during heavy KV write. Any trend on sequence length distribution? If recent traffic has longer contexts, kvcache pressure spikes.

Ana (SRE): running quick node checks now: `kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-48` and `dmesg | tail -n50`.

Ana (SRE): dmesg snippet:
```
[  1023.456789] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3e:00): 79, 0 GPU has fallen off the bus
[  1023.456799] NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:3e:00: GPU affinity lost
[  1023.457101] nouveau 0000:3e:00: pci_hotplug: link down
```

Oncall GPU: pods affected: model-a (2 replicas), model-b (1), preprocessor (1). Traffic currently being routed to spare pool but capacity reduced ~25%. Liz, any customer bridge?

Liz (Prod SE): opening a lightweight bridge with dmz customers we think are hitting model-a. Notifying 2 customers as impacted. No confirmed customer errors yet, just latency.

Kai (Runtime): recommended mitigation path:
1) cordon gpu-48
2) drain non-critical inference pods with `--ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30` to free GPU memory quickly
3) restart nvidia driver on the host and blow away stale GPU state if driver restart does not clear, plan a controlled node reboot

Ana (SRE): executing cordon now.
```
kubectl cordon gpu-48
kubectl drain gpu-48 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30 --timeout=5m
```

(30s later)

Ana (SRE): drain in progress, some pods stuck Terminating — runtime shows containers stuck cleaning up NV shared mappings. Trying `crictl` force remove.

Dev Patel: could be a hung kernel module state. If `rmmod nvidia` isn't possible, we'll need to reboot. Check `lsmod | grep nvidia` and `ps -ef | grep nvidia` to see if anything is holding.

Ana (SRE): `lsmod` shows nvidia and nvidia_uvm loaded; `rmmod nvidia_uvm` fails: "module is in use". Trying to identify PIDs holding /dev/nvidia* handles.

Ana (SRE): found processes: containerd-shim pid 4821 (model-a). Forcing container kill, then `rmmod nvidia_uvm` attempted again.

Oncall GPU: after kill and rmmod, driver restart attempted: `systemctl restart nvidia-driver` -> success?

Ana (SRE): driver restart logs show transient failures then success, but dmesg still shows Xid 79 events tailing in low volume. Behavior changed: resets less frequent but still present.

Kai (Runtime): with driver up, we should validate kvcache health. Rolling restart of runtime on this host to reinitialize caches (with lower concurrency) is safer than letting stale state linger. I'll coordinate a single-process restart for runtime service.

Dev Patel: take a snapshot of runtime metrics before restarting:
`curl -s http://localhost:9100/metrics | grep kv_cache`

Ana (SRE): snapshot saved to /var/tmp/gpu-48-kvcache-20260315.prom. Proceeding with runtime restart (graceful).

(1m)

Ana (SRE): runtime restarted, kvcache back to nominal, ECC corrections back to baseline. No more new Xid 79s in last 45s. Kubernetes node marked Ready.

Oncall GPU: traffic ramping back to normal; we still see ~10% error retries for model-a — probably warm-up. Putting node in maintenance and leaving cordon for 30m.

Liz (Prod SE): customer update: emailed impacted customers with ETA ~30-45m; offered to route to regional replica if they want immediate failover.

Customer Ops: confirming two customers accepted failover to us-west-1; no data loss reported. Monitoring closely.

Kai (Runtime): follow-up action items:
- Add a runtime guard: reject requests that would blow kvcache beyond safe threshold (soft limit) and return 429 to trigger client-side backoff
- Add alerting rule on `nv_xid_count` > 3 in 1m to page earlier
- Run targeted repro with long-context load on a test node to see if we can reproduce memory growth pattern

Ana (SRE): filing incident ticket INC-2026-03015 with timeline, logs, and decision to cordon+restart. Assigning to Kai for runtime changes and Dev Patel for driver-state runbook edits.

Ana (SRE): handing to follow-up (postmortem) owners; I'll monitor for 1 hour then release. If it recurs, escalate to full fleet recall.

Oncall GPU: thanks team. Closing active paging. Will update thread if anything flares up. :white_check_mark:
